A leasehold property is partially owned by the buyer for a pre–decided time period. The buyer owns the property, mostly a flat, but not the land on which it stands and is entitled to pay a ground premium and annual lease rent. After the expiry of the lease, the ownership of the property transfers to the freehold owner. In India, leasehold period normally goes up to 90–99 years.
